Alright, let me think through this year...

4.1 mu isn't much land, but it's what my father left and what's fed us all this time. I've worked it 25 years now. Wife's at home, older boy goes to do construction in Handan in winter — sends back some money — younger one's still in school. So there's a bit of outside cash, but not much. Everything we spend on seed and fertilizer has to come back out of the land.

I split the land the way I always do. About 2 mu in cotton — that's our money crop, same as most folks on this side of the county. Another 2 mu I keep in wheat through the winter, and then I push maize into it soon as the wheat comes off in June. That wheat gives us flour, and the maize we either sell or feed if we keep a pig. Leaves a little corner by the house, maybe 0.1 mu, for the wife's vegetables — I don't count that as proper farming.

**Cotton (2 mu).** I'll start in April. Get the same hybrid seed I've been buying at the shop in town — Old Wang and most of the village uses this one, it handles bollworm alright. Before planting, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — spread across the 2 mu. Then when it starts flowering, about July, I'll topdress urea, half a bag or so over the 2 mu. I can't put as much as the bigger farmers do. My wife's brother keeps telling me more fertilizer means more cotton, but the bag costs what it costs, and the cotton price is what it is. I'll spray for bollworm two times at least, maybe three if it's a bad year — that's the one thing you don't skimp on, because if the bolls get eaten there's nothing left. Water from the well maybe once in July and once in August if the rains don't come. Diesel's not cheap for the pump. Picking cotton — that's all us by hand, me and the wife, stretched over September and October. My boy helps when he's home.

**Wheat (2 mu).** Plant around middle of October, right after the maize is off. I hire the seeder from the village cooperative — cheaper than owning one. Before planting I spread a bag of compound on the 2 mu. Water it once to get it up. Then in winter if it's dry I'll water, and again in spring when it greens up I'll put urea down and water. One more watering at the filling stage if needed. Spray weeds in spring. Hire the combine from the cooperative in early June.

**Maize (same 2 mu, after wheat).** No time to rest — get the maize in within a week of the wheat coming off, or you lose heat at the end. I plant straight into the stubble with the seeder, urea and compound go in with the planting. Topdress more urea when it's about knee-high. Summer rains usually carry it but I'll water once if July turns dry. Spray herbicide early so weeds don't take over. Harvest late September — got to move fast to get the wheat back in.

What I worry about: cotton price has been jumpy the last few years, but I don't know what else to grow. I don't have the land or cash to try something new. The wheat-maize pays the food bill, the cotton pays for everything else. Same way I did it last year, same way my father did it. If it worked last year, no reason to change.
